newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling firm on dollar, maintains bull.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling firm on dollar, maintains bull.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling was firm against the dollar on Tuesday on excess dollar inflows carried forward from Friday, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 54.58 on the dollar compared to 54.62 on Monday while against the pound it was posted at a mean rate of 88.82 from 89.14.
The shilling's bullish tone has been sustained by regular flows from export sales and foreign investors amid amid desperately low levels of demand causing an unmatched market.
"It's currently trading at 54.40/70 levels," one dealer said. "We expect it to strengthen as proceeds from coffee and tea sales today come in today," the dealer added.
Dealers said the 54-figure level remained the next pychological barrier, a key test point for the shilling.
The money market was liquid with overnight rates unchanged between 5-10 percent.
